conviction_note: Q4 revenue should carry about $0.7m of SPAR Group revenue that the $6.02m consensus (+4.5% YoY on a flat base) does not appear to hold, so print_vs_bar is about +7%. But this name sold +11% and +7% growth prints (-10.5%, -8.8%) and bought a miss (+6.6%). The revenue comes from a company TRAK lends to and is paid in that company's OTC stock, and the bar has one source. So the +0.9 sum is emitted at +0.6: the reaction function and quality-of-beat discount take a third off, and the range is wide both ways.
bar: Q4 FY26 (quarter to 2026-06-30) consensus revenue $6.02m and EPS $0.09 from 3 analysts, FXEmpire (https://www.fxempire.com/stocks/trak/earnings). One source only; a search summary also mentioned $5.90m but could not be sourced. No company guidance exists (the Q3 call gave none). Unsourced by the two-source standard, so every size here is capped small. For reference, Q3 consensus was $6.21m / $0.11 and Q3 printed $5.883m / $0.10 (https://www.investing.com/news/transcripts/earnings-call-transcript-repositrak-q3-2026-misses-forecasts-but-sees-stock-rise-93CH-4690536).
positioning_check: Short interest about 1.4m shares at the 2026-09-15 FINRA settlement, days to cover 14.94, with an average of 17.3 days over 24 reports (https://www.optionsanalysissuite.com/stocks/trak/short-interest, snippet-level). The sweep had 11.2% of float and 14.17 days at 2026-08-31. That is persistently high rather than newly built. No usable option chain: skew is null and put/call OI is 0.23 on 137 contracts, so the market makes no directional statement. Tape: spot 8.24, flat over 5 and 20 days, -51% from the 52-week high, down about 22% since 1 June as the SPAR ties were disclosed. No negative finding is filed, so the crowded short only matters as a squeeze risk if the headline beats.

findings.finding: Q4 FY26 revenue should include roughly $0.58m of a $2,325,000 one-year SPAR Group services contract (term from 2026-03-13, invoiced in full and paid on 2026-05-29 in 3,190,569 SGRP shares), plus $151,500 from a new SPAR IT development agreement that runs from 2026-06-01. That is about $0.73m on a subscription base of about $5.87m, so revenue lands near $6.4-6.6m (+11-15% YoY) against the $6.02m bar, and EPS near $0.11-0.13 against $0.09.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Rebuilt from confirmed release dates because the baseline rows are off by one session. Q4 FY25, released 2025-09-29 amc: revenue +11%, called a revenue miss, stock -10.5% (16.56 to 14.82). Q1 FY26, 2025-11-13 amc: revenue +10%, +0.3%. Q2 FY26, 2026-02-17 amc: revenue +7%, -8.8% (10.09 to 9.20). Q3 FY26, 2026-05-14 amc: revenue flat, missing $6.21m by 5%, +6.6% (9.10 to 9.70) after a 12% slide the week before. Revenue beats have not been paid for here; the true median absolute reaction is about 7.6%, not the baseline's 2.52%.
findings.why_not_priced: The $6.02m consensus is only +2.3% on Q3's $5.883m. Q3's subscription line was $5,867,398, flat YoY (TRAK 10-Q, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/50471/000143774926017105/trak20260331_10q.htm). If the three analysts had modelled $0.7m of SPAR revenue, the bar would sit near $6.5m, or their core estimate would imply a 10% sequential drop, which nothing supports. The IT development agreement ($151.5k a month) appears only in SPAR's 10-Q, not in any TRAK filing or release. Management did not quantify SPAR revenue on the Q3 call and said the impact would come in '6 to 9 months'. What cuts against it is already inside the number: the size assumes ratable recognition, the analysts may have partly modelled it, and a reader who strips related-party revenue paid in OTC stock sees a flat core. That quality discount and the reaction history are why this is +0.8 and not a multiple of it. Net of the rest of the company: the core subscription base (about 90% of revenue) has to hold near $5.8-5.9m; a repeat of Q3's slip would take about $0.1m off.
findings.independence: TRAK's own 8-K of 2026-06-03 independently confirms the $2,325,000 one-year services agreement and the stock payment (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/50471/000143774926019434/trak20260603_8k.htm). The IT development fee rests on the SPAR 10-Q alone.

findings.finding: Below the operating line, Q4 carries a fair-value gain on the 4,190,569 SGRP shares held at 30 June: cost about $3.125m (3,190,569 at $0.7287 plus 1,000,000 at $0.80), worth about $3.48m at the $0.83 close on 2026-06-30. That is about $0.35m, plus roughly $60k of 8% interest on the $3.0m note to SPAR Marketing Force. Together they add about $0.02 to EPS.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior below-the-line item on this name to measure against; the stock has moved on revenue.
findings.why_not_priced: The inputs (a 14.8% SGRP stake per the 13G, the note terms in the 10-Q, SGRP's OTC price) sit in three separate places no preview joins. The dollar amount is tiny and the gain has no path to guidance, so it is sized as a fraction of its EPS equivalent. It may also be booked on the equity method or at a different basis.
findings.independence: SGRP daily closes (https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/SGRP?period1=1780012800&period2=1783036800&interval=1d). Note terms and the 1,000,000-share consideration come from TRAK's Q3 10-Q (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/50471/000143774926017105/trak20260331_10q.htm). This rests on the same SPAR relationship as finding 1 but on a different line and different documents.

outside_window.finding: From FY27 Q1 SPAR revenue runs at about $1.03m a quarter ($0.58m services plus $0.45m IT development), about 17% of revenue. The 31.4% SGRP stake (13D event date 2026-07-01, partly funded by a $2.57m 6% note to the seller) moves to equity-method accounting, and $1.0m more of the SPAR loan was drawn on 2026-07-15. All of it shows in the Q1 FY27 report, not this one, except insofar as management discusses it on the call.

searched_and_found_nothing: Financing: the $35m universal shelf with ATM language (S-3 filed 2026-08-25, S-3/A 2026-09-24, EFFECT 2026-09-25) is the three-year renewal of the August 2023 shelf (S-3 2023-08-11, S-3/A 2023-08-23 and 08-24), filed at the same point in the cycle. Cash about $26m, no bank debt, stated use is general corporate. No corroborated raise, so it is sized at 0 (https://www.sec.gov/cgi-bin/browse-edgar?action=getcompany&CIK=0000050471&type=S-3&dateb=&owner=include&count=20; https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/50471/000143774926028873/trak20260824_s3.htm)

Insider trades: the only 2026-08 Form 4 is the CFO's 75,000-share restricted grant under his new employment agreement (8-K 2026-08-18). No open-market cluster (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/50471/000148372826000002/form4-08262026_040834.xml)

FSMA 204: compliance and enforcement stay at 2028-07-20. The rule is unchanged and there was no new FDA action in summer 2026 (https://www.fda.gov/food/food-safety-modernization-act-fsma/fsma-final-rule-requirements-additional-traceability-records-certain-foods)
Touchless Retail deployment (2026-09-17) and the SPAR launch (2026-08-18) are both on the wire and carry no quantified revenue

SPAR governance: two Brown-aligned directors were pushed out on 2026-08-06 and the board cut to five. No ReposiTrak role is named and there is no in-window TRAK impact (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1004989/000143774926027309/sgrp20260812_8k.htm)

Baseline reaction history: every row is off by one session because it keys on 8-K or 10-Q filing times, not the release. The history was rebuilt from releases and daily closes (https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/TRAK?period1=1758672000&period2=1759622400&interval=1d and the matching Nov 2025, Feb 2026 and May 2026 windows)
baseline_tension: There is no skew to agree or disagree with. The stock is 51% off its high and has drifted down 22% since June as the SPAR entanglement was disclosed. A headline beat built on SPAR revenue is exactly what that selling has been discounting, so the positive read is emitted smaller than its sum.
lessons_applied: Lesson 2 (one-offs as one-offs): the SGRP mark-to-market and loan interest finding was cut from +0.3 to +0.1, since it is below operating income with no path to guidance.
Lesson 3 (caveat reaches the number): the quality-of-revenue counterweight in finding 1 was already resolved into one sign. The emitted move is +0.6 against a +0.9 sum, and the note says why.

Lessons 1 and 6 (reaction veto, unsourced bar) left finding 1 at +0.8. The reaction history rebuilt per the 'wrong events' lesson shows growth sold, and the bar has one source, so the fact is not upsized.
Lesson 8 (thin coverage moves more) was weighed and not applied as an upsize, because the revenue recognition timing is inferred rather than confirmed. It is reflected in the wide -4/+6 band.
Lesson 4 (financing is a question): answered before the draft. The shelf is a renewal of the 2023 shelf and stays at 0.
